provider_query: Python standard library documentation for the venv module
answer:
Official and closely related sources for Python’s standard-library `venv` module:

1. **Library reference (current stable-style docs)** — `venv` creates lightweight virtual environments on top of a base Python install, isolated by default from system site-packages. Covers CLI (`python -m venv`), options (`--system-site-packages`, `--symlinks`/`--copies`, `--clear`, `--upgrade`, `--without-pip`, `--prompt`, `--upgrade-deps`, `--without-scm-ignore-files`), and the `EnvBuilder` API. Added in 3.3.  
   https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html

2. **Versioned library reference (3.14)** — Same module page pinned to Python 3.14.1.  
   https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/venv.html

3. **Tutorial: Virtual Environments and Packages** — Beginner walkthrough: why venvs exist, `python -m venv`, common `.venv` layout, activation on Windows vs Unix/macOS (including csh/fish), and using the env with `pip`.  
   https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/venv.html

4. **Tutorial source (CPython repo)** — RST source for the tutorial chapter above.  
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/HEAD/Doc/tutorial/venv.rst

5. **Implementation** — `Lib/venv/__init__.py` in CPython (PEP 405-based `EnvBuilder` and CLI).  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Lib/venv/__init__.py

6. **pydevtools handbook summary** — Concise overview: stdlib since 3.3, comparison with virtualenv and uv, maintenance notes (e.g. `--upgrade-deps` in 3.9; setuptools no longer installed by default in 3.12).  
   https://pydevtools.com/handbook/reference/venv/

7. **Using a specific interpreter** — Practical note that the env uses the Python that runs `python -m venv` (e.g. `python3.12 -m venv .venv` or `py -3.12 -m venv` on Windows), plus the common “No module named venv” fix on minimal Debian/Ubuntu (`python3.x-venv`).  
   https://www.pythontutorials.net/blog/how-do-i-use-different-python-version-in-venv-from-standard-library-not-virtualenv/

8. **Create / activate / remove walkthrough** — Short tutorial on directory layout (`pyvenv.cfg`, `bin`/`Scripts`, `Lib/site-packages`) and linking to the official docs for full flags.  
   https://python.land/virtual-environments/virtualenv
